verses.1: O lords, please grant justice and equality to your servants. You know that you also have a lord in heaven.
verses.2: In this prayer, please be patient, as you will find comfort in it through your prayers.
verses.3: Praying also for ourselves, that the Lord may open to us the door to the Word, so that we may speak of the mystery of Christ. Through this, we can be freed from our bonds.
verses.4: To show them how I must speak.
verses.5: In wisdom, you should move towards those outside, taking advantage of the opportunities that arise from time.
verses.6: Your words are always full of wisdom; they are like stones that have been carefully arranged. It’s clear how each of you should respond to them.
verses.7: All that I have to say will be known to you. May your beloved brother and faithful servant be fortunate. He is also a loyal supporter and companion in the Lord.
verses.8: I have sent him to you here, so that you may know about us and ask for your hearts’ desires.
verses.9: With your faithful and beloved brother, who is among you; everything related to you will be known to them.
verses.10: The Aristarchus, my fellow laborer, and the honest Márkos Barnabas will take care of you. You may give them orders when they come to see you.
verses.11: And Jesus, who was called “Jehovah”. Those who were born from circumcision—these alone are true partners in the kingdom of God. They have been my guides and helpers.
verses.12: Epaphras, one of you, a slave of Christ, always fights for your sake in prayers, so that you may become perfect and fully equipped for every good thing that God has prepared for us.
verses.13: I testify to him that he suffers greatly for your sake, as well as for those in Laodicea and in Hierapolis.
verses.14: You are being taken over by Lucius, the beloved doctor, and Demas.
verses.15: You have taken possession of the brothers in Laodicea, along with Nympha, and also the church that was located in their house.
verses.16: And when the letter is read before you, do so that it can also be read in the synagogue of Laodicea. And you should read it from Laodicea as well.
verses.17: And you said to Archippus: “Look at the duties that you have received from your master, and fulfill them.”
verses.18: The kiss from Paul’s hand for me. Remember my bonds. It is a gift from you.
